items.claim: A screenshot-style endpoint that hands the user-supplied URL straight to a headless browser navigation is a source-review-confirmable SSRF sink, and the only gate on it is a scheme allow-list plus a non-empty-domain check.
items.body:
A screenshot-style endpoint that hands the user-supplied URL straight to a headless browser navigation is a source-review-confirmable SSRF sink, and the only gate on it is a scheme allow-list plus a non-empty-domain check.

HackTricks reference: 30f098c3 (notion:30f098c3-95c5-8076-b9f0-fe0fbc805cd9)
items.disproof: The URL parameter is never passed to an outbound fetch or browser navigation, or it is resolved and rejected against internal ranges before use.

sources.quote: If an attacker cannot directly contact a target, but the product has access to the target, then the attacker can send a request to the product and have it be forwarded to the target. The request would appear to be coming from the product's system, not the attacker's system.
In general, basic SSRF (when the response is returned to the attacker), is easier to exploit than Blind SSRF in which the attacker has no feedback on whether or not the attack was successful.

items.claim: Allow-listing only the http/https scheme is the baseline SSRF filter that blocks file: URLs, and any filter 'improved' on top of it is a candidate for probing with simple obfuscation of localhost before escalating to DNS rebinding.
items.body:
Allow-listing only the http/https scheme is the baseline SSRF filter that blocks file: URLs, and any filter 'improved' on top of it is a candidate for probing with simple obfuscation of localhost before escalating to DNS rebinding.

HackTricks reference: 30f098c3 (notion:30f098c3-95c5-8076-b9f0-fe0fbc805cd9)
items.disproof: Obfuscated loopback hostnames and the file: scheme are both still rejected and no internal response or local file content comes back.

items.claim: A domain check that only runs its private-range test when the input parses as an IP literal leaves a gap: any hostname that resolves to a loopback address passes the filter and still reaches 127.0.0.1.
items.body:
A domain check that only runs its private-range test when the input parses as an IP literal leaves a gap: any hostname that resolves to a loopback address passes the filter and still reaches 127.0.0.1.

HackTricks reference: 30f098c3 (notion:30f098c3-95c5-8076-b9f0-fe0fbc805cd9)
items.disproof: The application resolves the supplied hostname and re-checks the resolved address, so a localtest.me-style name is rejected and the request never reaches loopback.
